record.title: TRACE reports accountable retrieval gains on one OCR-degraded French historical archive benchmark
record.summary: Bian et al. introduce TRACE, a training-free agentic retrieval system designed for OCR-degraded, heterogeneous historical archives. On HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic, 1,752 French-language questions over BnF-derived parliamentary debates and newspapers from 1887, the authors report overall R@10 0.856 and multi-gold MRR 0.653, above tested BM25, dense, graph-based and agentic RAG baselines. Its components include corpus-targeted query decomposition, fused sparse/dense/temporal retrieval, explicit accept/reject/hold verdicts with deferred re-evaluation, and cross-sub-question reranking. The paper reports roughly $0.02 per question under its hosted-inference configuration and an internal project prototype accessible to 24 researchers across six institutions. These are author-reported results on one corpus; code was not run, and adoption, expert workload, trust and transfer beyond the 1887 French setting remain unmeasured.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic (1,752 questions over 3,386 French documents from 1887), the authors report TRACE R@10 0.856 and multi-gold MRR 0.653 using DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report higher overall R@10/MRR than tested BM25 (0.643/0.467), dense retrieval (0.734/0.535), HippoRAG 2 (0.737/0.453), LinearRAG (0.727/0.513), A-RAG (0.385/0.211) and MA-RAG (0.586/0.356).

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For TRACE, the authors report accepted-set precision 0.393 and recall 0.879 overall, and a cumulative ablation in which decomposition, memory/replanning, warm start and hold/re-evaluation add 8.9%, 2.4%, 5.0% and 0.5% R@10 respectively.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors estimate approximately $0.02 per question for DeepSeek-V4-Flash under the reported hosted-inference configuration; a 200-question timing sample averaged 33.8 LLM calls and 169 seconds of model time per question.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report an internal DECIDON research prototype accessible to 24 researchers across six partner institutions; measured adoption, expert reading burden and workflow impact are deferred.

evidence_gaps.description: The benchmark, code and reported costs were not independently reproduced in this review.
The evaluation covers one French historical corpus/year; transfer to other periods, languages and archival genres is untested.
Traceability is designed into returned results, but user trust, verification effort, adoption and workflow impact are not measured.

brief.importance_rationale: If reproduced across archives and languages, corpus-aware agentic retrieval with inspectable source paths could change how institutions screen digitized collections for scholarly research at modest hosted-inference cost. Current evidence is a single author-reported French 1887 benchmark and does not establish reduced expert effort, broader transfer or production outcomes.
limitations: Results are author-reported; the public code was not run and no independent reproduction was performed.
The benchmark covers 1,752 questions over one 1887 French historical corpus and does not establish transfer to other periods, languages or archival genres.
The agentic baselines do not return ranked document lists; ranking their discovery trajectories is generous in one respect and asymmetric in another, as the paper notes.
TRACE reports approximately $0.02 per question for one hosted-inference configuration; token pricing, call count and latency are provider/configuration dependent.
An internal prototype is not a production deployment; adoption, historian trust, verification effort and workflow impact remain unmeasured.
brief.summary: Bian et al. introduce TRACE, a training-free agentic retrieval system designed for OCR-degraded, heterogeneous historical archives. On HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic, 1,752 French-language questions over BnF-derived parliamentary debates and newspapers from 1887, the authors report overall R@10 0.856 and multi-gold MRR 0.653, above tested BM25, dense, graph-based and agentic RAG baselines. technical.claimed_result: A training-free, corpus-aware agentic retrieval pipeline can improve ranked source discovery and accepted-set precision/recall over tested sparse, dense, graph-based and agentic baselines on a noisy historical archive benchmark.
technical.compute_or_cost: The authors report $36 hosted cost for DeepSeek-V4-Flash over 1,752 questions, approximately $0.02 per question; their 200-question timed sample averaged 33.8 calls and 169 seconds of model time per question. These depend on the stated provider prices and configuration.
technical.demonstrated_result: The authors report overall R@10 0.856, multi-gold MRR 0.653 and accepted-set precision/recall 0.393/0.879 over 1,752 questions, plus approximately $0.02 per question for their hosted DeepSeek-V4-Flash configuration. These are paper-reported results and costs, not independently reproduced.
technical.mechanism: TRACE decomposes a query into corpus-targeted subquestions; fuses sparse BM25, dense, temporal and exact-string retrieval; alternates search and explicit accept/reject/hold review; carries compact memory and replans between subquestions; then merges and reranks documents by cross-subquestion confirmation and recorded rationales.
technical.regime: HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic: 1,752 questions over 3,386 French-language parliamentary-debate and newspaper documents from 1887, split into 5,664 chunks. Baseline comparisons use a shared converted corpus and common backbones/embeddings where applicable. The prototype is an internal DECIDON service, not production.
technical.reproducibility: The paper links a public GitHub repository whose README identifies an MIT license, CLI, JSONL corpus/question inputs, optional embedding cache and hosted/local-model configuration. No benchmark data files or release appeared in the repository root listing, and no pinned-commit execution was performed; reproduction remains open.
technical.strongest_baseline: Dense retrieval is the strongest simple overall baseline in the reported table (R@10 0.734, MRR 0.535); graph and agentic systems use the paper’s specified adaptations and ranking protocol.

brief.title: TRACE reports accountable retrieval gains on one OCR-degraded French historical archive benchmark
brief.why_it_matters: Historical and institutional retrieval needs relevant documents with inspectable paths back to evidence, especially when OCR errors and mixed sources defeat simple search. TRACE reports that orchestration and corpus-aware retrieval can improve document discovery on one French historical benchmark without training a new model. The benchmark does not show that TRACE reduces historian workload or transfers to other archives.
